legend: Axial T2-weighted MRI shows a mass in the right ischioanal fossa (shown here, arrow). Coronal T2-weighted MRI (Fig. <<56231>>) shows that the mass ascends through the pelvic floor into the pelvis with a typical swirled/layered appearance. T2 high-signal areas (asterisk) are commonly encountered due to myxoid matrix.

Low-power view showing a hypocellular tumour with fibromyxoid matrix. Interspersed vessels are seen uniformly scattered within the lesion.
Higher-power view showing spindled to stellate cells with delicate cytoplasmic processes. Collagen fibrils and smooth muscle (myoid) bundles may be seen spinning off the vessels.

A hypocellular tumour with fibromyxoid matrix and spindled to stellate cells having delicate cytoplasmic processes.  Interspersed vessels are seen uniformly scattered within the lesion. Collagen fibrils and smooth muscle (“myoid”) bundles may be seen in close proximity to the vessels.
